newsitem.title: JAPAN: Planned NTT unit would halt losses in 3 yrs -- MPT.
newsitem.headline: Planned NTT unit would halt losses in 3 yrs -- MPT.

text.p: The Posts and Telecommunications Ministry (MPT) said on Wednesday it believed the weaker of the regional telecom operators to emerge from the break-up of Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp would be able to halt losses within three years after NTT's restructuring.

"We believe that the regional carrier covering western Japan will overcome losses within three years," a senior ministry official said in response to a question at a Lower House parliamentary telecommunications committee.

Late last year, the ministry and NTT agreed on a plan under which NTT would be split up into two regional carriers -- one to cover eastern Japan and the other to cover western Japan -- and one international and long-distance carrier under a holding company. The plan needs parliamentary approval before it can be carried out.

An NTT official told the panel that if NTT were to be broken up in 1999, the regional carrier for eastern Japan would post a profit of 110 billion yen while the one for western Japan would post a loss of 100 billion yen in the year from April 1, 1999.
In 2000/01, the firm covering eastern Japan would post a profit of 130 billion yen and the western Japan company would post a loss of 80 billion yen, the official said.
The NTT restructuring plan allows the carrier covering eastern Japan to use its profits to offset possible losses at the other regional carrier for three years after the break-up.
"The expected loss at the western Japan carrier would be only temporary as it includes costs stemming from the restructuring," the ministry official said.
The regional companies would try their best to cut costs and improve their services so that there would be no difference between their call rates, NTT president Junichiro Miyazu told the panel.
